subject: mathematics

grade_and_subject.standards_system_name: B.E.S.T. Standards (Benchmarks for Excellent Student Thinking)

domains.domain_name: Number Sense and Operations: Understand the place value of three-digit numbers

standards.text: Read and write numbers from 0 to 1,000 using standard form, expanded form and word form.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compose and decompose three-digit numbers in multiple ways using hundreds, tens and ones. Demonstrate each composition or decomposition with objects, drawings and expressions or equations.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Plot, order and compare whole numbers up to 1,000.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Round whole numbers from 0 to 100 to the nearest 10.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Number Sense and Operations: Add and subtract two- and three-digit whole numbers

standards.text: Recall addition facts with sums to 20 and related subtraction facts with automaticity.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify the number that is ten more, ten less, one hundred more and one hundred less than a given three-digit number.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Add two whole numbers with sums up to 100 with procedural reliability. Subtract a whole number from a whole number, each no larger than 100, with procedural reliability.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explore the addition of two whole numbers with sums up to 1,000. Explore the subtraction of a whole number from a whole number, each no larger than 1,000.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Fractions: Develop an understanding of fractions

standards.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal-sized parts. Name the parts using appropriate language, and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds or four fourths.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Partition rectangles into two, three or four equal-sized parts in two different ways showing that equal-sized parts of the same whole may have different shapes.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Algebraic Reasoning: Solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 100 and related subtraction problems

standards.text: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Algebraic Reasoning: Demonstrate an understanding of equality and addition and subtraction

standards.text: Determine and explain whether equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation, relating three or four whole numbers, with the unknown in any position.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Algebraic Reasoning: Develop an understanding of multiplication

standards.text: Represent an even number using two equal groups or two equal addends. Represent an odd number using two equal groups with one left over or two equal addends plus 1.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Use repeated addition to find the total number of objects in a collection of equal groups. Represent the total number of objects using rectangular arrays and equations.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Measurement: Measure the length of objects and solve problems involving length

standards.text: Estimate and measure the length of an object to the nearest inch, foot, yard, centimeter or meter by selecting and using an appropriate tool.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Measure the lengths of two objects using the same unit and determine the difference between their measurements.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Solve one- and two-step real-world measurement problems involving addition and subtraction of lengths given in the same units.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Measurement: Tell time and solve problems involving money

standards.text: Using analog and digital clocks, tell and write time to the nearest five minutes using a.m. and p.m. appropriately. Express portions of an hour using the fractional terms half an hour, half past, quarter of an hour, quarter after and quarter til.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems involving either dollar bills within $100 or coins within 100¢ using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geometric Reasoning: Identify and analyze two-dimensional figures and identify lines of symmetry

standards.text: Identify and draw two-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes. Figures are limited to triangles, rectangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons and octagons.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Categorize two-dimensional figures based on the number and length of sides, number of vertices, whether they are closed or not and whether the edges are curved or straight.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify line(s) of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geometric Reasoning: Describe perimeter and find the perimeter of polygons

standards.text: Explore perimeter as an attribute of a figure by placing unit segments along the boundary without gaps or overlaps. Find perimeters of rectangles by counting unit segments.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Find the perimeter of a polygon with whole-number side lengths. Polygons are limited to triangles, rectangles, squares and pentagons.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Data Analysis and Probability: Collect, categorize, represent and interpret data using appropriate titles, labels and units

standards.text: Collect, categorize and represent data using tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs. Use appropriate titles, labels and units.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Interpret data represented with tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs including solving addition and subtraction problems.
standards.label: A

key_learning_outcomes.label: C
items: Students read, write, compose, compare, and plot whole numbers up to 1,000 and round numbers from 0 to 100 to the nearest 10.
Students recall addition facts to 20 and add and subtract within 100 with procedural reliability, and explore addition and subtraction within 1,000.
Students partition circles and rectangles into halves, thirds, and fourths.
Students solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction problems, including length, time to the nearest five minutes, and money within $100 or 100 cents.
Students identify and categorize two-dimensional figures, find perimeter, and collect and interpret data in tables and graphs.
